title: Cold-start next and status output is difficult to scan
symptom: The next action is buried in very large JSON output
trigger: Run chough next and chough status --json on the repository checkpoint with its existing evidence history
expected: A fresh agent can identify the native and session actions without manually inspecting thousands of lines
actual: next emitted 11567 JSON lines in 16 seconds and status emitted 11568 JSON lines in 36 seconds, including full native content and observation records
steps: Capture command output and count the lines
impact: Cold resume is slow and the important contradiction is easy to miss

notes.text: The read-only chough timing command also took about 233 seconds and emitted 51507 bytes; plan, test and human-gate histories had too few samples. This is additional output-size and performance friction, not work included in this change

Correction to the original actual field: both next and status emitted 11567 JSON lines, not 11568 for status. The reviewer counted the JSON payload boundaries in the preserved scratch capture; the timing-output note is unchanged
The original Kimi cold-start observation supplies failed evidence for this finding; its recorded scope and open status are unchanged
The retrospective scope-gate observation preserves the same original failure on the completed draft content; scope and open status are unchanged
